rule: Silken threads boiled in sea-water yield mire-essence
texts: Each Keeper takes the sea-water from the Salt-bloom Tide-pools.

mixed: the rule fires and every participant is carried (each Keeper, the taking, the sea-water, the source), but "the Salt-bloom Tide-pools" is recorded as one named individual of kind tide-pool — a capitalised multi-word name has no way to say the referent is several pools, so the plurality of the source is lost. If the plural matters, lowercase the common-noun head so it parses as an ordinary definite plural tied to the name: "Each Keeper takes the sea-water from the Salt-bloom tide-pools."

rule: Hunted nightmoths flee to dimmer lights
texts: Whenever a sky-cat hunts at a lantern-row, each nightmoth that survives the hunt moves to the Hollows.

(: whenever_hunt_move (Implication (And (Member $x sky_cat) (Member $h hunt) (Agent $h $x) (Member $y lantern_row) (Location $h $y) (Member $m nightmoth) (Member $s survive) (Agent $s $m) (Theme $s $h)) (And (Member (sk_move $h $m) move) (Agent (sk_move $h $m) $m) (Goal (sk_move $h $m) hollows) (During (sk_move $h $m) $h))) (STV 1.0 0.9))

good. parses as a fireable whenever-rule: the sky-cat's hunt, its lantern-row location and the surviving nightmoth are all plain matchable conditions, and a move to the Hollows is minted per hunt-and-moth pair with all participants covered.

rule: Sky-cats molt feathers to the cliff base
texts: Each Keeper stores the collected feathers in a bin at the Watch.

(: each_keeper_stores (Implication (Member $x keeper) (And (Member (sk_store $x) store) (Agent (sk_store $x) $x) (Theme (sk_store $x) sk_feathers_1) (Member (sk_bin $x) bin) (Location (sk_store $x) (sk_bin $x)) (LocatedIn (sk_bin $x) sk_watch_1))) (STV 1.0 0.9))

good. parses as a fireable per-Keeper rule with everything covered: the collected feathers as one definite set with "collected" handed to each feather, and each Keeper's own bin, itself placed at the Watch.

rule: Spring tides occur near new moon and full moon
texts: Each Keeper times the salt-bloom harvest to the new-moon spring tide.

bad: "times X to Y" has no slot that fits — the parse files "to the new-moon spring tide" as a spatial destination for the timing event, asserting that something travels to the tide, which the sentence never says; the only licensed alternative (the bare "to" oblique) would instead feed the purpose machinery and derive an aim the sentence never states. Say the alignment with a plain temporal clause instead, splitting the scheduling and the timing into two finite clauses: "Each Keeper schedules the salt-bloom harvest, and the harvest happens during the new-moon spring tide."
Whenever a cliff-spire shields a cove against north winds, each lantern in that cove burns stably through winter.
Whenever a cliff-spire shelters a cove, each lantern in that cove stays lit through winter.

(: whenever_shield_burn (Implication (And (Member $e shield) (Agent $e $cs) (Member $cs cliff_spire) (Theme $e $cv) (Member $cv cove) (Against $e north_wind) (Member $l lantern) (LocatedIn $l $cv)) (And (Member (sk_burn $e $l) burn) (Patient (sk_burn $e $l) $l) (Manner (sk_burn $e $l) stably) (Through (sk_burn $e $l) winter) (During (sk_burn $e $l) $e))) (STV 1.0 0.9))

(: whenever_shelter_lit (Implication (And (Member $x cliff_spire) (Member $sh shelter) (Agent $sh $x) (Member $c cove) (Theme $sh $c) (Member $l lantern) (LocatedIn $l $c)) (And (Member (sk_lit $l) lit) (Experiencer (sk_lit $l) $l) (Still (sk_lit $l)) (Time (sk_lit $l) winter) (During (sk_lit $l) $sh) (Member $l lit))) (STV 1.0 0.9))

good. it becomes a fireable rule that triggers on any cliff-spire/cove pairing, keeps the north-wind shielding as part of the condition, and gives each lantern its own burning event with the manner and the winter span attached. One limitation no rewrite avoids: "through winter" is recorded as a plain preposition on the burning, so its span sense (all winter long) is not marked as an extent.

mixed: the rule fires and every participant is present, but "stays lit" becomes a single lit-state per lantern that is then said to hold during every sheltering episode, so one state is shared across all occasions instead of one per occasion — incoherent as soon as two shelterings are in play. Use the shape of your own first sentence instead: a plain finite verb in the consequent rather than the copular "stays". Rewrite as: "Whenever a cliff-spire shelters a cove, each lantern in that cove burns through winter." — for a lantern, burning through winter is exactly staying lit through it, and that pattern parsed cleanly in the first sentence.

rule: Large feather stores enable safe Sunken-Cove tending
texts: When the feather store at the Watch is large, each Keeper tends the Sunken Cove lanterns safely in winter.

(: store_large_keeper_tend (Implication (And (Member sk_store_1 large) (Member $x keeper)) (And (Member (sk_tend $x) tend) (Agent (sk_tend $x) $x) (Patient (sk_tend $x) sk_lanterns_1) (Manner (sk_tend $x) safely) (Time (sk_tend $x) winter))) (STV 1.0 0.9))

good. faithful and fireable — the largeness condition, the each-Keeper universal with its quantifier record, the manner "safely", the winter time, and the Sunken Cove lanterns as one group all come through. Worth knowing rather than fixing: the condition is tied to the one specific store this sentence introduces, so the rule fires only when a later statement about that same store is resolved to the same store.
Whenever a wraith drains a lantern at the Sunken Cove, a station near the Sunken Cove requests feather rations from the Council.
When a station reports a drained lantern, the Council prioritizes that station.

(: whenever_drain_request (Implication (And (Member $x wraith) (Member $d drain) (Agent $d $x) (Member $l lantern) (Patient $d $l) (LocatedIn $l sunken_cove)) (And (Member (sk_request $d) request) (Agent (sk_request $d) sk_station_1) (Theme (sk_request $d) feather_ration) (Source (sk_request $d) sk_council_1) (During (sk_request $d) $d))) (STV 1.0 0.9))

(: station_report_prioritize (Implication (And (Member $e report) (Agent $e $s) (Member $s station) (Theme $e $l) (Member $l lantern) (Member $l drained)) (And (Member (sk_prioritize $e) prioritize) (Agent (sk_prioritize $e) sk_council_1) (Theme (sk_prioritize $e) $s) (During (sk_prioritize $e) $e))) (STV 1.0 0.9))

bad: the consequent's "a station near the Sunken Cove" is lifted out of the condition — the parse asserts outright that such a station exists and sits near the cove, and it fixes one and the same station as the requester for every draining, neither of which your sentence claims; separately, "at the Sunken Cove" attaches to the lantern rather than to the draining, so the rule keys on where the lantern sits. Rewrite as: "Whenever a wraith drains a Sunken Cove lantern, the station near the Sunken Cove requests feather rations from the Council." — the definite "the station" makes the one standing station the stated reading, so asserting it is licensed, and "a Sunken Cove lantern" ties the cove to the lantern with no attachment ambiguity left.

good. it becomes a fireable rule that triggers on any station's report, treats "drained" as a property of the lantern rather than a second event, and hands that same reporting station to the Council's prioritizing — nothing lost.
